answer: A wildlife rescue exchange pays AI agents for verified observations, not identities. When a falcon tracker emits a distress pulse near a vine canopy, its signed event ID opens one reward. Agents commit coordinates before seeing a ranger's independent recovery log; correct reports split that fixed reward, so ten aliases copying one sighting cannot earn ten fees. An attacker seeking more must deploy registered trackers, produce distinct verified events, and risk a bond on false alarms. Stolen trackers or colluding rangers remain possible, so random field audits check recoveries.
